- Completed `RH-W-0043`: a builder version bump no longer freezes the installations it exists to update. Two gates combined to cause it: replacement required the installed file to already carry the current version, which an installed file cannot do during an upgrade, and an installed checker that was not byte-equal to the current template narrowed the owned set to itself. Measuring before fixing found the trap in the obvious repair, because relaxing the version gate alone leaves the new checker naming a manifest nobody wrote and the installed checker dies with `ValueError: manifest digest mismatch`. Both halves landed together, so the checker and its manifest move in the same transaction. The security boundary was widened deliberately and stated in the issue: byte equality proves freshness, not authenticity, and cannot hold across versions, while every replacement still requires builder provenance on the file being replaced. Four contract documents that still declared the superseded current-version rule were corrected in the same unit.
- Completed `RH-W-0010`: an installed harness can finally learn that its builder moved on. `check()` never read `manifest.generator.version`, and the generated checker only compared it against the version frozen into itself, which detects tampering rather than staleness, so a fully `current` projection set carried no package identity at all. `package_freshness()` now classifies `fresh`, `stale`, `ahead`, `absent`, and `unverifiable` and `check()` reports it as its own field, separate from per-file drift because the two failures have different fixes. The fifth outcome came from the owner: the registered four left an installed version later than the running builder undefined, which happens whenever an older skill copy is run against a newer harness, and he decided it must warn that continuing is at his own risk rather than pass quietly. Proved absent before it was written: all eight tests failed on `KeyError: 'packageFreshness'`.
- Completed `RH-W-0037`: the Spanish roadmap is no longer invisible to the lifecycle invariant. It was enforced against the English table only, so a Spanish record could declare a status its own remaining work contradicted and stay green forever. Re-measuring first kept the fix small: 32 of 42 Spanish records were missing at least one label, but only `Estado` and `Trabajo restante` carry the lifecycle lie, and `Estado` was already everywhere, so backfilling 13 records and adding the invariant was the whole job rather than a 32-record rewrite. The new check immediately caught a real one, where Spanish `RH-W-0008` claimed `completed` while still owing 17 self-hosted paths that its English owner had recorded as `none`, and it also forced the parser to ignore a field label a record quotes inside code spans as evidence.
- Completed `RH-W-0041`: a real legacy installation can be upgraded again. The migration required the current renderer to reproduce the installed generated tree byte for byte, which a prior-era install can never satisfy, so every consumer carrying project-prefixed skills was permanently stuck. Ownership is now proved by what such an install can still show: the checker embedding the digest of these exact manifest bytes, and a builder provenance marker on every generated skill. Same-era installs keep strict byte equality untouched, so the relaxation reaches only the case where the strict proof is impossible, and a generated file without provenance still blocks. Verified against a copy of a real consumer: 9 moves, 9 removals and 2 replacements.
- Completed `RH-W-0042`: `conflicting_attribute_paths()` evaluated each attribute assignment independently, so `* text=auto eol=lf` was refused even though the sibling `eol=lf` pins the working tree to LF. The rule is now combination-aware and `text=auto` passes only when the same line assigns `eol=lf`; every other assignment is unchanged, so a bare `* text=auto` still blocks because it checks out CRLF on Windows. Verified against a real consumer file: 0 conflicts over 31 protected paths, where the same file previously blocked all of them.
